q6.answer: The Order service is the coordinator: it drives each step by HTTP calls to Inventory and Payment and by reacting to Payment events. The record of progress is the Order's status field in the Order database (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID_PENDING_CLAIM, CONFIRMED, etc.). There is no separate orchestrator or saga table.

q7.answer: The provider sends a webhook to the Payment service, the only service that talks to the provider. Payment records the outcome and publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event on the broker, which Order consumes to update the order status and continue.

q8.answer: Payment stores each provider event id under a unique constraint, in the same transaction as the resulting state change. A repeat finds the id already recorded, returns 200 OK and does nothing. Order also applies status changes only from an allowed previous status, so re-delivered broker events are harmless.

q9.answer: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined, Order sets CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and emails the customer, and Order publishes an OrderCancelled event. Inventory consumes that event and releases the hold so the stock goes back on sale. If the hold has already lapsed, the release does nothing.

q10.answer: On PaymentSucceeded, Order asks Inventory to claim the hold, and Inventory does an atomic conditional update from HELD to CLAIMED. If the hold is still HELD the claim succeeds and the order is confirmed. If it was already RELEASED the claim is refused, so Order cancels as out of stock and requests a full refund from Payment. Claim and expiry race on the same row and whichever commits first wins.

q11.answer: The refund stays PENDING and is retried with backoff, using its own idempotency key (refund + order id). After the retry limit it becomes FAILED_NEEDS_ATTENTION, operations are alerted, and it stays on a manual retry list, never deleted. It is tracked in the Payment service's database in a refund record with status, attempt count, next retry time and last error. The exact retry count and backoff schedule were not decided and are left as an open point.

q12.answer: The Cart service empties the cart when it receives the OrderConfirmed event, which Order publishes when the order reaches CONFIRMED. The cart is not emptied on any failure. Whether to empty the whole cart or only the snapshot's lines (in case the customer added items while waiting) was left as an open decision.
